analysis:
The only change in this PR is a one-line documentation edit to the gpt_oss row of the model table in docs/architecture/inference.md (head line 1163). It states that a bf16 checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamps with scalar bounds that take the activation dtype. The supplied units (head lines 1-807) are surrounding documentation only. The changed line itself is outside the displayed excerpt, but the patch excerpt shows it in full. No code, configuration, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache-scope or coordinator/provider protocol change is made. The surrounding text covers Nemotron Super serving, the prefix cache and deadlines; it is unchanged and describes existing behavior.

Relevant threat-model touchpoints are TB-007 and T-041 (prefix cache). The gpt_oss row's reference to the default-on SSD cache for gpt-oss-20b is unchanged. The new statement concerns numeric dtype handling, not at-rest artifacts, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, scope derivation or salt folding.

I identified no security regression, no new attack surface, and no invalidated threat-model assumption. The dtype claim is documentation about an SDK source file (GPTOSS+Experts.swift) that is not supplied, so its accuracy is unverified. It is a correctness and doc-accuracy matter, not a security conclusion. Future code changes that alter KV dtype could affect the SSD cache layout binding and the layoutEpoch fail-closed checks under T-041. This PR makes no such change.
